transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 09:38 AM PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Evan Clarke (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), John Reyes (Hawthorne CTO), Priya Nair (Hawthorne Infra Lead), Samir Patel (Hawthorne Sec Ops)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Hawthorne is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a reserved GPU deployment to serve internal LLM-powered research and client-facing risk-scoring models. Primary concerns: data isolation, burst/baseline capacity, predictable latency under business hours spikes, and compliance (SOC2, KMS). Next steps: pricing + SLA, tech deep dive to validate throughput and network topology, share security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Evan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:00:05] John: Yeah good morning. Hearing you Evan.
[00:00:10] Priya: Morning, good to meet you all.
[00:00:15] Maya: Hi all, Maya from Redwood, I'll jump into the technical bits after Evan covers context.
[00:00:22] Evan: Cool, quick agenda — we'll run through what hawthorne is trying to do, talk Dedicated versus Hosted, dig into capacity/burst questions, then Maya will do a short tech Q&A.
[00:00:33] John: Sounds good, from our side short intro — we run pricing/risk models for private wealth clients, moving to LLMs for summarization and some automated Q&A. Latency is important, cost matters but predictability and data isolation are the top two.
[00:00:50] Samir: Also security, we can't have PII leaving our VPC and need audit logs.
[00:00:56] Evan: Understood. So Dedicated is our reserved capacity option, full isolation from multi-tenant pools, you get dedicated GPU pools and network controls - you can choose a VPC peering or private link, plus KMS integration.
[00:01:12] John: What's the typical sizing and granularity? We need baseline for daytime 200 concurrent requests with bursts to 2k during earnings / reporting windows.
[00:01:24] Maya: For that profile we usually recommend reserving a baseline of N GPUs depending on model and sequence length — for example a 70B dense model might map to 8-12 A100-style equivalents for steady throughput; bursts can be handled via burst capacity that Redwood can autoscale to, but bursts are throttled by available capacity and warm-up times.
[00:01:46] Priya: When you say burst capacity, is that in the same Dedicated pool or do you route to Hosted? We need guaranteed isolation for certain workloads.
[00:01:55] Evan: Good question — we offer two burst modes. 1) Burst-in-pool: you've reserved N GPUs and we can overprovision temporarily within your dedicated pool assuming spare hardware in the region, 2) Cross-pool burst/fallback: for non-sensitive workloads we can route to a hosted compatibility model for overflow. For workloads that must stay isolated, you should plan capacity headroom or apply a burst contract.
[00:02:18] Samir: So if we hit an extreme spike, our sensitive calls will be queued or slowed unless we pre-commit more. That's acceptable; we just need clear SLOs.
[00:02:26] Maya: Exactly, we can set latency SLOs per route and apply admission controls. Also we support KV cache prefixing to reduce tokens for repeated context which helps cost and latency during spikes.
[00:02:38] John: How about model variants — can we fall back to smaller quantized models within the same Dedicated environment?
[00:02:45] Maya: Yes, we support multiple model variants on the same Dedicated cluster, you can configure routing policies to use a quantized variant under high load. Note quantized models may slightly affect quality for some tasks.
[00:02:58] Priya: Network topology question: we run in AWS in us-east-1 with strict egress controls. Can Redwood Dedicated be deployed in our VPC or do we have to use a managed VPC?
[00:03:08] Evan: We have a Private deployment option where the control plane is customer-managed and compute sits in your VPC via peering/PrivateLink; for Dedicated hosted we offer VPC peering and private networking that respects your egress rules. Maya, add anything?
[00:03:20] Maya: If you need full on-prem or air-gapped we also have an on-prem package, but that's a bigger project. For most infra teams VPC peering + dedicated pools gives the isolation you want while keeping control plane in Redwood.
[00:03:33] Samir: KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM?
[00:03:38] Maya: Yes, we integrate with AWS KMS CMKs and can support HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest. Audit logs for every request can be pushed to your S3/CloudWatch for retention.
[00:03:48] John: Latency target — we need 95th percentile < 150ms for small prompts, 500ms for 2k-token responses is okay. Realistic?
[00:03:58] Maya: For small prompts and with a tuned model and batching disabled for low-latency routes, 95p < 150ms is achievable on proximate dedicated GPUs — depends on model size and KV cache warm state. For long generation the 500ms depends on decode speed, token rate, and model size. We should run benchmarks with your actual prompts.
[00:04:16] Evan: We'll propose a benchmark run in the tech deep dive. We typically do a daylight spike simulation and capture p95/p99 across route configs.
[00:04:23] Priya: What's the typical warm-up time for a cold KV cache or model spin-up when scaling up?
[00:04:29] Maya: Model warm-up is typically seconds to a couple minutes depending on model size and whether weights are cached; KV cache build-up depends on request patterns. For autoscaling we rely on preforking and caching strategies to reduce cold starts.
[00:04:42] John: Pricing — how do you charge? Flat reserved fee plus usage for bursts? Anything for dedicated networking?
[00:04:49] Evan: Pricing is a mix. Dedicated has a reserved monthly commit for the baseline capacity, plus metered usage for burst/overage. Networking add-ons (private link, peering) are usually pass-through or a small platform fee depending on the contract. We'll send a detailed pricing deck.
[00:05:03] Samir: Do you provide cost controls and token-level reporting? That's important for us to attribute spend to business units.
[00:05:09] Maya: Yes, Console has token-level cost, per-route breakdown, and tagging support so you can get per-product/unit cost attribution.
[00:05:16] John: For our compliance path we need SOC2 / ISO certs, SSO via SAML, RBAC, and data residency controls.
[00:05:24] Evan: We have SOC2 Type II, we can share the report under NDA. SAML SSO and RBAC are supported, and data residency can be met by choosing region-specific Dedicated pools or Private deployments.
[00:05:35] Samir: Do you maintain request-level logs including full prompt/response? That's sensitive; we may only want metadata.
[00:05:42] Maya: You can configure log retention and redaction; for sensitive data we recommend redaction on ingestion and route-level policies to avoid storing PII.
[00:05:51] John: Ops — who runs upgrades and how disruptive are rolling restarts to the Dedicated pool?
[00:05:56] Maya: Upgrades are orchestrated with canaries and automatic failover to minimize disruption. You can opt into scheduled maintenance windows. For Dedicated we do live rolling upgrades and provide maintenance SLAs.
[00:06:07] Evan: Quick qualification: what's your expected timeline to purchase?
[00:06:11] John: We're targeting a Q2 pilot, production in H2 if benchmarks are good. Decision maker is my CEO and the infra committee.
[00:06:18] Evan: Budget ballpark?
[00:06:20] John: We have initial budget carved ~$250k/year for baseline plus extra for benchmarks and reserves.
[00:06:27] Priya: For the benchmark what artifacts do you need from us?
[00:06:30] Maya: Sample prompts, typical sequence lengths, concurrency profile, and representative payload sizes. Also network topology and egress constraints so we can architect peering.
[00:06:40] Samir: We'll send a redacted sample set.
[00:06:43] John: Ok. One more Q: can we have separate Dedicated clusters per BU for strict isolation while sharing management?
[00:06:52] Evan: Yes, you can have multiple Dedicated pools under a single account with role-based access, or separate accounts if you want full tenancy separation.
[00:06:59] Priya: What's the SLA for Dedicated uptime and latency?
[00:07:03] Evan: We offer SLA-backed uptime >99.9% for Dedicated, with latency SLOs configurable per route and financial remedies in enterprise contracts. We'll include the SLA language in the deck.
[00:07:12] Maya: Also note backups and model snapshotting for rollback are supported - important for canary rollouts.
[00:07:18] John: Any red flags from your side about our setup?
[00:07:21] Maya: Just that for strict throughput you may want to size for 20-30% headroom for bursts unless you want to rely on cross-pool fallback. Also quantify acceptable quality delta if you plan to use quantized variants for cost saving.
[00:07:35] Evan: We'll follow up with a recommended capacity estimate and cost scenarios (baseline only, baseline+burst contract, baseline+cross-pool fallback).
[00:07:43] Samir: I need the SOC2 and SSO details to share with our auditors.
[00:07:47] Evan: I'll send those under NDA.
[00:07:50] John: Great. Anything else?
[00:07:53] Maya: Quick note — we can do a 2-week POC on Dedicated if you want to validate latency and p95 under load; it typically requires a small reserved commit and test harness.
[00:08:03] John: Let's plan for the tech deep dive first, then POC if results look good.
[00:08:08] Evan: Recap of action items and next steps: Evan send pricing + SLA + SOC2 (Evan), Maya schedule tech deep dive and benchmark plan (Maya), Samir share security questionnaire and SSO/KMS details (Samir).
[00:08:22] Priya: Thanks all, we'll review and get back with best times for the deep dive.
[00:08:27] Evan: Thanks everyone.
[00:08:30] John: Bye.

(notes: transcription contains occasional mishears; example: "K V cache" instead of "KV cache" in a few spots, and vendor names transcribed as RunCloud instead of RunDeck in one mention)
